newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia battle flares on eve of ASEAN peace trip.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia battle flares on eve of ASEAN peace trip.

text.p: Government forces under Hun Sen captured a base from troops loyal to ousted premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh in northwestern Cambodia on Friday and thousands of civilians fled into neighbouring Thailand to escape the fighting.
The flare-up on the battlefield came as an Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) delegation prepared to make a return to Phnom Penh for a second attempt to help solve Cambodia's crisis.

Thai military officials on the border with Cambodia said Hun Sen's forces seized a royalist position at O'Bei Choan, northeast of the Cambodian border town of Poipet, after a battle lasting several hours.
Up to 6,000 Cambodian civilians fled into Thailand as Thai authorities opened the border due to the severity of the clash.
"They really needed to escape the fighting," one Thai official said.
There was no word on casualties and military authorities in Phnom Penh said they were awaiting a report on the situation.

The ASEAN team arriving in Phnom Penh for talks on Saturday will be made up of the same men who flew to Phnom Penh and tried unsuccessfully to launch a mediation effort two weeks ago -- foreign ministers Ali Alatas of Indonesia, Prachuab Chaiyasan of Thailand and Domingo Siazon of the Philippines.
Alatas said on Friday the ASEAN team would offer ideas to Cambodian strongman Hun Sen on ways to resolve the political crisis.

"The three ASEAN foreign ministers will convey ideas on how we can contribute to a settlement of the Cambodia crisis," Alatas told reporters in Jakarta. "We want to see how to restore political stability in Cambodia."
He declined to give details of the proposals to be made.
Second Prime Minster Hun Sen ousted his co-premier, Prince Norodom Ranariddh, on July 6 after two days of battles in Phnom Penh and bluntly rejected all attempts to mediate in the crisis.
Cambodia's troubles dominated a recent ASEAN foreign ministers' meeting in Kuala Lumpur.
The grouping was thrown into confusion by conflicting signals from Cambodia over whether or not the Hun Sen-controlled government would welcome a mediation effort.

Cambodian Foreign Minster Ung Huot said on Friday his government would discuss peace and stability with the ASEAN mission but suggested the grouping should not interfere in Cambodia's internal affairs.
"Anything that is not interference in our internal problems we can accept," Ung Huot told reporters.

But diplomats in Phnom Penh said they were optimistic there would be some progress in Saturday's talks and said Ung Huot's remarks could be diplomatic posturing and were not necessarily a rejection of any role for ASEAN.

Fighting between troops loyal to the rival premiers erupted in parts of Cambodia after Ranariddh's ouster with Hun Sen's men pushing the royalists back to remote areas of the north and northwest of the country.

Cambodia's Khmer Rouge guerrillas, who ousted their notorious leader Pol Pot last week, have said they support Ranariddh and have vowed to unite with all anti-Hun Sen forces and "destroy" his government.

A Khmer Rouge military commander told the Far Eastern Economic Review in a report published this week that Pol Pot, responsible for the death of more than a million people during his 1975-79 rule, was purged because of his opposition to an alliance with the royalists.
Hun Sen has threatened military action against the Khmer Rouge and said Pol Pot must be tried by an international court.

As thousands of Cambodians were taking refuge in makeshift camps in Thailand to escape the fighting, King Norodom Sihanouk warned in published remarks that his country was in danger of becoming the long-term "sick man" of Asia.

"I am very upset by such a destructive and destabilising evolution for my country, Cambodia, now considered and I fear irredeemably for many years to come as the 'sick man' of Asia," the king wrote in a letter to Reporters sans Frontieres (Reporters without Borders), a Paris-based media watchdog.
Sihanouk, Ranariddh's, father is in Beijing for medical treatment.
